summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain following a five-day polysubstance binge involving alcohol, cocaine, and heroin. He had a high blood alcohol level and positive urine toxicology for opioids. Evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction with normal troponins and unchanged EKG. The chest pain was deemed atypical and likely related to alcohol and opioid withdrawal, though hypertension may have contributed. He was treated with Valium for withdrawal, restarted on lisinopril and other cardiac medications, and started on Imdur for blood pressure. Metoprolol was held due to recent cocaine use. The patient decided to leave against medical advice after being counseled on the risks. He was provided with rehab resources and instructed to follow up with his primary care physician.
